sections.normalized_html: There are some special types of square matrices.
sections.readable_text: There are some special types of square matrices.

sections.normalized_html:
• A square matrix is called diagonal, if all entries that do not lie on the main diagonal (from top-left to bottom-right) are zeros. For example, the following matrices are all diagonal matrices: [MATH: [1|0; 0|1]] Note that we can have any number (including [MATH: 0]) on the diagonal.

  • An identity matrix is a diagonal matrix where the entries on the diagonal are all [MATH: 1]'s (and all other entries are [MATH: 0]'s). For example, the following matrices are all identity matrices: [MATH: [1]] We use the notation [MATH: I_n] for the [MATH: n \times n] identity matrix.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Some important types of matrices have special names.

Content:
- An [MATH: m \times n] matrix in which all entries are zeros is called a zero matrix. For example, the following matrices are both zero matrices:
[MATH: [0|0; 0|0; 0|0]]
We use the notation [MATH: O_{m \times n}] to represent the zero-matrix with [MATH: m] rows and [MATH: n] columns. So, the zero matrices shown above are [MATH: O_{3 \times 2}] and [MATH: O_{2 \times 2},] respectively.
- A [MATH: n \times n] matrix (meaning the number of rows equals the number of columns) is called a square matrix. For example, the following matrices are square matrices of dimensions [MATH: 2\times 2] and [MATH: 3\times 3,] respectively:
[MATH: [a|b; c|d]]

---

Item 2 — Example: Identifying a Zero Matrix

Example Prompt:
Which of the following are zero matrices?
[MATH: [0|0; 0|0]]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
- [MATH: P] is a zero matrix since all its entries are zeros.
- [MATH: Q] is not a zero matrix since some of its entries are not zeros (for instance, [MATH: q_{12}=0.1\neq0]).
- [MATH: R] is a zero matrix since all its entries are zeros.

Therefore, only [MATH: P] and [MATH: R] are zero matrices.

---

Item 8 — Tutorial: Diagonal, Identity, and Other Matrices

Content:
There are some special types of square matrices.

Content:
- A square matrix is called diagonal, if all entries that do not lie on the main diagonal (from top-left to bottom-right) are zeros. For example, the following matrices are all diagonal matrices:
[MATH: [1|0; 0|1]]
Note that we can have any number (including [MATH: 0]) on the diagonal.
- An identity matrix is a diagonal matrix where the entries on the diagonal are all [MATH: 1]'s (and all other entries are [MATH: 0]'s). For example, the following matrices are all identity matrices:
[MATH: [1]]
We use the notation [MATH: I_n] for the [MATH: n \times n] identity matrix.

Content:
Finally, as we've seen before:

Content:
- If a matrix has only one row, then it's called a row vector. An example of a row vector is shown below.

- If a matrix has only one column, then it's called a column vector. An example of a column vector is shown below.
